note: "Left United States, San Francisco, California." The narrative history has the arrival on 14 October; the chronology 20 October; Building the Navy's Bases 21 October (bases-24). No record found names the ship. A candidate, by its dates (inferred; no record of the battalion names her): the U.S. Army Transport President Coolidge sailed from San Francisco about 1100 on 6 Oct 1942 and "reached Noumea on the morning of October 20th, and discharged some navy personnel and their cargo", sailing on the afternoon of 24 Oct for Espiritu Santo, where she sank on mines on 26 Oct (the 172nd Infantry's history, NAID 404300670 p368: a destroyer and a dirigible "for the first half day; for the remainder of the voyage the transport was unescorted"). An officer aboard: she "had discharged approximately 1500 CBs with their gear and equipment at Noumea" (Espiritu Santo command history, NAID 77638874 p15), more than the first wave's 591 men, so she probably carried other Seabee units too.
"Left united States, Port Hueneme, California. (San Pedro, California)." The card dates the second wave's departure 26 November (ncbhist-020/p2). No record found names the ship.

ships: LST-334, LST-390, LST-446, LST-447, LST-448, LST-449; escorts SANDS and HUMPHREYS (Task Unit 32.6.2)
carried: "Acorn FIVE; Naval Base Unit; and, one half of the 20th Naval Construction Battalion"
note: Commander Amphibious Force, South Pacific's war diary: departed Nouméa 1600 local on 14 May 1943, arrived Townsville 0800 local on 20 May. Which half of the 20th went in which LST isn't recorded.

ships: McCAWLEY and PRESIDENT ADAMS, of Transport Division Two (Task Unit 32.8.2: PRESIDENT JACKSON, PRESIDENT HAYES, PRESIDENT ADAMS, McCAWLEY, LA SALLE), with six destroyers
carried: McCAWLEY: 70th Coast Artillery Unit, Naval Base personnel unit, 20th Naval Construction Battalion. PRESIDENT ADAMS: Naval Base personnel unit, 20th Naval Construction Battalion and 429th Signal Construction Company.
note: Transport Division Two's war diary logs the flagship's position at 0800, 1200 and 2000 each day (voyage_positions.csv). Japanese air raids were expected on 10 June; the destroyers' report of the action that evening is in an annex. Which of the two ships a man was in isn't recorded.

carried: LST 354 - 800 tons of equipment for 20th Construction Battalion to North Renard, RUSSELL I.; LCT 62 and 133 - 150 tons each
note: Commander Task Group 32.3's war diary (cargo delivered 12 June 1943). The craft that carried the men aren't named.

ships: Seven LCIs (serials 1A-1G) and an LCT (serial 1N); with APDs WARD and SCHLEY carrying the Marine raiders
carried: LCIs: 20th C.B., 3 officers, 100 men, hand tools and demolition equipment to prepare the beaches for the LCTs. LCT 1N: 20th C.B. (less 1/2 Co), 3 officers, 128 men and 1,345 sq. ft. of vehicles
note: The Eastern Force loading order of 16 June 1943: loaded at Wernham Cove and the north side of Renard Sound on D-1 day (29 June), landed at Oleana Bay on D-day (30 June), Rear Admiral Fort commanding. A plan, not a record of what sailed; Rentz has the convoy off Oloana Bay at 0335 on 30 June (mcsol). Next day LCT 367 delivered 1 officer, 60 men and the 20th's vehicles and LCT 481 40 men and 161 tons (rg38-78141899/p0007).

ships: An LCI (serial 1U) and an LCT (serial 2J); the first echelon in APDs HOPKINS, ZANE, KILTY and CROSBY
carried: LCI 1U: Det Co "D", 20th C.B., 1 officer, 50 men, hand tools and demolition equipment. LCT 2J: 1/2 Co "D", 20th C.B., 3 officers, 62 men and 1,240 sq. ft. of vehicles
note: The loading order: the LCI to land at Viru on D-day, the LCT on D plus 1. The landing at Viru was delayed: Building the Navy's Bases has the first echelon land on 2 July (bases-25).

ships: LCT-145 and LCT-146, escorted by APc 37 and APc 42
carried: "one-half company of 20th Construction Battalion" (Oliana to MUNDA); 3 officers, 114 men (ncbhist-020/p11)
note: Commander Task Group 31.3's war diary of 8 September 1943 orders the two LCTs, loading at Oliana, to Munda; his monthly summary lists "20th Construction Battalion (1/2 company) Wickham to MUNDA", 125 men and 200 tons. The chronology has them leave Vangunu on 9 September and reach Bau Island on 10 September.

ships: APc 45 and LCT 367; LCTs returning from Torokina
note: Commander Task Group 31.3's war diary, 28 and 30 December 1943: APc 45 and LCT 367 on their way to Ondonga to load the 20th; the returning Torokina LCTs to complete the move from Ondonga to the Russells about 7 January. The Bau Island group (4 officers, 211 men) sailed on 9 January in craft not named.
One stop at Guadalcanal. No record found names the ship.
A man was left at the dispensary at Eniwetok on 26 February (rg24-190273312/p0698). No record found names the ship.

ships: Four LSTs (ncbhist-020/p12), two of them LST-824 and LST-898; convoy of LST Group 67 (flagship LST-802): 8-9 LSTs, 6 LSMs and 6 LCS(L)s with 4 destroyer escorts
carried: LST-824: 210 enlisted men and 6 officers, and CB equipment of the 20th NCB. LST-898: 250 men with gear and 8 officers of the 20th USN Construction Battalion
note: LST-824's war diary logs its position at 0800, 1200 and 2000 each day (voyage_positions.csv); it had loaded pontoon barges at Guam. The convoy was the first into Chimu Wan; LST-898 beached at its western end on 19 April and disembarked the Seabees; LST-824 finished unloading its "CBs passengers" on 20 April. The other two LSTs aren't named.
No record found names the ship.
The card: CAPE BON departed 2 Feb 1945 with the battalion, routed via Pearl Harbor and Saipan.
